card.name: Small words right after -ly adverbs
card.fires_on: A preposition or punctuation mark that comes right after an adverb ending in -ly, such as concomitantly, thoroughly, gently or frequently. It is strongest on "with" after "concomitantly" in drug-interaction text.

modes.label: with after concomitantly
modes.description: The word "with" directly after "concomitantly" in interaction statements.

modes.label: Other words after -ly adverbs
modes.description: A preposition or punctuation mark after an adverb such as thoroughly, gently, promptly or frequently, in instructions or monitoring text.
modes.example: mucosa thoroughly<< with>> water. Visually inspect parenteral drug
